Edouard Glissant was a writer and philosopher from Martinique, best known for his ideas of Antillanite, creolisation and the poetics of relation. He wrote novels, poems and essays.

A student of Aime Cesaire's generation, he moved beyond Negritude, which looked to Africa, to stress the mixed, creole identity formed in the Caribbean from many sources. His novel The Ripening (1958) won the Prix Renaudot.

His work inspired the Creolite movement of younger Martinican writers such as Patrick Chamoiseau, and is read widely in Caribbean and postcolonial studies. He taught in Paris and New York.
